raw_segments.text: The French, under the old monarchy, held it for a maxim, which is still a fundamental principle of the English Constitution, that the King could do no wrong. And if he did do wrong, the blame was imputed to his advisers. This notion was highly favorable to habits of obedience, and it enabled the subject to complain of the law without ceasing to love and honor the lawgiver. The Americans entertain the same opinion with respect to the majority.
